text:
Carol will likely win, because the seller misdescribed the car as a 1964 model when it was a 1968. An "as is" clause disclaims implied warranties but not express ones, and the ad's description of the car became part of the basis of the bargain (UCC 2-313). The team note that fault or carelessness is required is wrong, since express warranty liability is strict and doesn't depend on negligence. Of the choices, D is the closest fit, though A is the other plausible pick.

CONFIDENCE: 66
